title: Cohomology is the colimit of Cech cohomology over hypercoverings
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file hypercovering.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Deduce from theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings that H^i(F) is the colimit of the Cech groups over all hypercoverings: replace C by a slightly bigger site C' with a final object X - call sheaf-surjective families weak coverings, define C' explicitly (objects of C plus X, morphisms to X, weak coverings and the X-coverings, restricted via sets-lemma-coverings-site), and note Sh(C') = Sh(C) because C -> C' is special cocontinuous; choose a covering K_0 of X by C-objects, set K_init = cosk_0(K_0); for (1) apply the theorem in C' to get K' -> K_init with xi coming from Cech cohomology, write K'_n = {U_{n,j}} with U_{n,j} in C, and unwrap K back into SR(C) as a hypercovering in the definition-hypercovering-variant sense (weak coverings of C are coverings of C'), concluding by equality of the Cech complexes; for (2) transfer K and L into C', enlarge coverings for the set-theoretic issue, apply the theorem to obtain M' -> K', L', K_init and unwind.
